description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training set, comprising 13 distinct slices, each representing a specific data source with corresponding labels, colors, and percentage values. The largest segment is NQ, which accounts for 31.3% of the dataset, followed by FEVER at 16.1%, SNLI at 15.4%, and MULTINLI at 11.3%. VITAMINC contributes 13.0%, while SCITAIL makes up 1.2% and MULTIFC 0.5%. The smallest contributors are SCIFACT at 0.1% and PUBHEALTH at 0.5%, with ENFRA at 1.8%, FACTCC at 2.6%, and ANLI at 4.6%. The slices are color-coded and labeled with lines pointing to their respective percentages, with the largest slices positioned toward the top-right and smaller ones distributed around the chart. The visual layout emphasizes the dominance of NQ and FEVER, while the minor contributions of SCIFACT and PUBHEALTH are clearly distinguishable due to their small size and placement.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training set, comprising 13 slices. Each slice represents a specific data source with distinct labels, colors, and percentage values. The largest data source is NQ, accounting for approximately 31.3% of the dataset, followed by FEVER at 16.1%. SNLI and MULTINLI are the next largest contributors, with 15.4% and 11.3%, respectively. Notably, VITAMINC shows a steady decline in its contribution compared to previous years, now accounting for only 8.0% of the dataset. Additionally, SCIFACT and PUBHEALTH are among the smallest contributors, with SCIFACT slightly exceeding PUBHEALTH at 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each data source in the training set.
